consumer_contract: Every step names a native viewer_cameras entry using exact visibility; source text supplies mechanism and omissions. No runtime animation or physiology simulation.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Distinguish vascular perfusion from extracellular exchange with osteocytes.

steps.text: Identify periosteal and medullary supply landmarks.
steps.schematic_cue: Supply landmarks; connection continuity remains to be validated.
steps.native_camera: Function perfusion diffusion 1: Identify periosteal and medullary supply landmarks.

steps.text: Perforating channels house vessels linking cortical canal systems and surface supply.
steps.schematic_cue: Canal envelope and vessel lumen are different compartments.
steps.native_camera: Function perfusion diffusion 2: Perforating channels house vessels linking cortical canal systems and surface supply.

steps.text: Show the vessel pair inside the central canal. The nerve is another canal occupant.
steps.schematic_cue: Separate blood within vessel lumens from connective tissue around them.
steps.native_camera: Function perfusion diffusion 3: Show the vessel pair inside the central canal. The nerve is another canal occupant.

steps.text: Solutes reach osteocytes through pericellular extracellular fluid surrounding cells and processes. Diffusion operates in this network.
steps.schematic_cue: Captioned exchange concept; no particle crossing of an authored endothelial barrier.
steps.native_camera: Function perfusion diffusion 4: Solutes reach osteocytes through pericellular extracellular fluid surrounding cells and processes. Diffusion operates in this network.

steps.text: Identify venous drainage landmarks without inventing a capillary bridge or a proven continuous medullary route.
steps.schematic_cue: Separate arterial and venous instructional circuits.
missing_components: Capillary bridge between displayed artery and vein
steps.native_camera: Function perfusion diffusion 5: Identify venous drainage landmarks without inventing a capillary bridge or a proven continuous medullary route.

functional_sequences.scale_note: Vessels and channels are enlarged teaching constructions; no transit time, pressure, perfusion fraction or universal 200-µm osteon diameter is assigned.
schematic_limitations: No moving blood cells in Canaliculi.
V11 route report omits complete canalicular courses and complete medullary vascular continuity.
Do not animate geometry-following particles until saved-lumen connectivity has been verified.

functional_sequences.mechanism: External load can alter lacunar-canalicular fluid motion and osteocyte signals regulating formation.

steps.text: Introduce external mechanical loading as a conceptual cause.
steps.schematic_cue: Label optional external arrows schematic; leave geometry static.
steps.native_camera: Function osteocyte load sensing 1: Introduce external mechanical loading as a conceptual cause.

steps.text: Cyclic load-associated fluid displacement can enhance solute exchange.
steps.schematic_cue: Double-headed qualitative arrow; direction and amplitude are not geometry-derived.
steps.native_camera: Function osteocyte load sensing 2: Cyclic load-associated fluid displacement can enhance solute exchange.

steps.text: Focus on an osteocyte and its processes as the mechanosensitive cellular network.
steps.schematic_cue: Distinguish cell/process from the surrounding fluid gap.
steps.native_camera: Function osteocyte load sensing 3: Focus on an osteocyte and its processes as the mechanosensitive cellular network.

steps.text: Experimental loading reduced osteocyte Sost/sclerostin; unloading increased expression.
steps.schematic_cue: Caption-only molecular regulation.
steps.native_camera: Function osteocyte load sensing 4: Experimental loading reduced osteocyte Sost/sclerostin; unloading increased expression.

steps.text: Reduced inhibitory signaling can favor a local formation response.
steps.schematic_cue: Relate existing surface cells to the signal concept without inventing a visible pathway.
steps.native_camera: Function osteocyte load sensing 5: Reduced inhibitory signaling can favor a local formation response.

functional_sequences.scale_note: Displayed osteocytes are sparse and enlarged 1.30 times. Canalicular lumen display diameter is 1.04 µm; rat 0.15–0.17 µm reference is comparative only.
schematic_limitations: The fetched murine FRAP study is an experiment on ex vivo tibiae; its fitted velocity/shear estimates are not human model parameters.
No computed strain, fluid velocity, calcium transient, remodeling rate or mechanical adaptation.
External loading does not imply every osteocyte responds identically.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Relate the osteon axis, matrix organization and variable collagen directions qualitatively.

steps.text: Orient the concentric matrix around the longitudinal central canal.
steps.schematic_cue: Axis marker is explanatory.
steps.native_camera: Function lamellar mechanics 1: Orient the concentric matrix around the longitudinal central canal.

steps.text: Recognize the lamellae as mineralized collagen matrix.
steps.schematic_cue: A/B colors label representative groups rather than literal tissue colors.
steps.native_camera: Function lamellar mechanics 2: Recognize the lamellae as mineralized collagen matrix.

steps.text: Inspect the enlarged fibre illustration in the telescoped osteon.
steps.schematic_cue: Disclosure separation is artificial and fixed.
steps.native_camera: Function lamellar mechanics 3: Inspect the enlarged fibre illustration in the telescoped osteon.

steps.text: Native human sublamellar orientation can change smoothly, with oscillating and twisted patterns within one osteon.
steps.schematic_cue: Two sets simplify native complexity.
steps.native_camera: Function lamellar mechanics 4: Native human sublamellar orientation can change smoothly, with oscillating and twisted patterns within one osteon.

steps.text: Return to the interstitial and circumferential matrix as context for load-bearing tissue.
steps.schematic_cue: Discuss orientation-dependent structure qualitatively, without a numerical mechanical prediction.
steps.native_camera: Function lamellar mechanics 5: Return to the interstitial and circumferential matrix as context for load-bearing tissue.

functional_sequences.scale_note: Fewer displayed bands represent groups of native lamellae. Native 4–6 µm figure belongs to cited human femoral-section context; display band width is not that measurement.
schematic_limitations: No finite-element solver, elastic constants, torsion metric or fatigue/crack propagation computation.
Perfect A/B helix alternation is not claimed to describe all native human lamellae.
Telescoping is not physiological movement or interlamellar sliding.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Teach cellular resorption and replacement, distinguishing trabecular surface remodeling from cortical tunneling.

steps.text: Identify cells at a resting internal bone surface.
steps.schematic_cue: Surface context; a cell type need not be active at every displayed site.
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 1: Identify cells at a resting internal bone surface.

steps.text: An attached multinucleated osteoclast separates mineral dissolution from proteolytic matrix removal.
steps.schematic_cue: Highlight the cell and recess; caption the subcellular machinery absent from geometry.
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 2: An attached multinucleated osteoclast separates mineral dissolution from proteolytic matrix removal.

steps.text: A cortical BMU excavates a tunnel. This is distinct from the surface recess currently occupied by the displayed osteoclast.
steps.schematic_cue: Conceptual cortical-BMU caption; do not relocate the actual surface cell and claim it is a cutting cone.
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 3: A cortical BMU excavates a tunnel. This is distinct from the surface recess currently occupied by the displayed osteoclast.

steps.text: Human Haversian sections show reversal/osteoprogenitor recruitment interspersed with later resorption before formation.
steps.schematic_cue: Reversal boundary is visible; the mixed active cell population is not.
missing_components: Reversal/osteoprogenitor cells in a cortical BMU
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 4: Human Haversian sections show reversal/osteoprogenitor recruitment interspersed with later resorption before formation.

steps.text: Osteoblasts deposit osteoid; mineralization follows rather than being instantaneous.
steps.schematic_cue: Show final bands with a caption; no mesh growth or active mineralization front is authored.
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 5: Osteoblasts deposit osteoid; mineralization follows rather than being instantaneous.

steps.text: The replaced cortical region retains a central canal, while older lamellar remnants remain between newer osteons. Some formation cells become embedded osteocytes or lining cells.
steps.schematic_cue: Architecture and cell fates; no timed lineage transformation.
steps.native_camera: Function remodeling 6: The replaced cortical region retains a central canal, while older lamellar remnants remain between newer osteons. Some formation cells become embedded osteocytes or lining cells.

functional_sequences.scale_note: Steps compress a biological process lasting weeks to months into an untimed lesson. Cell density is representative; no formation rate or BMU advance speed is implied.
schematic_limitations: Existing Osteoclasts (Howship lacunae) occupy trabecular surfaces, not an authored cortical cutting cone.
No time-varying resorption cavity, osteoid formation or mineralization mesh.
No disease mechanism, endocrine setpoint or mass-balance simulation.
